title: Finite spectrum of a finite-type field algebra forces maximal primes
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $B$ be a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], allowing $B=0$. If $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has finitely many prime ideals, then every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal (equivalently, $\dim B\le0$).

source.place: Lemma 0ALW (finite type algebra with finitely many prime ideals), equivalence of (1) and (2)

proof.text: Fix a prime ideal \$\mathfrak p\subset B\$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal], \$\mathfrak p\$ is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. There are only finitely many such maximal ideals because \$\operatorname{Spec}B\$ is finite. If \$\mathfrak p\$ were not maximal, each of these maximal ideals would strictly contain \$\mathfrak p\$; choose \$x_{\mathfrak m}\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak p\$ for each one. Their finite product lies in every \$\mathfrak m\$, hence in their intersection \$\mathfrak p\$, while primality of \$\mathfrak p\$ implies that one factor \$x_{\mathfrak m}\$ lies in \$\mathfrak p\$, a contradiction. Thus every prime is maximal. If there are no maximal ideals above \$\mathfrak p\$, the cited intersection is the whole ring, so it cannot equal the proper prime \$\mathfrak p\$; hence the finite family is nonempty. The zero ring has empty spectrum, so the conclusion is vacuous there.
